parsed_output.evidence: Root cause / sink: obr/src/main/java/org/apache/karaf/obr/command/util/FileUtil.java, method copy() at line 171 — `new File(targetDir, destName)` — writes an OutputStream to a path built from archive-entry-derived strings (destName, destDir) with no re-validation at the point of the actual write. Trust boundary: destName/destDir/targetDir originate from JarEntry.getName() of an archive supplied to FileUtil.downloadSource()/unjar() (an OBR command/CLI can point at an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced remote/local archive URL), i.e. untrusted archive content crossing into the local filesystem-write sink. The only containment guard is in unjar() at line 113: `target.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(dir.getCanonicalPath())` — this string-prefix check has no path-separator boundary, so a sibling directory whose name extends the root's name (e.g. root "extract" vs sibling "extractEVIL") passes the check while resolving fully outside the intended root. Two source-to-sink paths in the alert both terminate at this same copy() sink and must both be covered by a fix: (1) trace via je.getName() -> name (line 134) -> destName (line 140/145) -> new File(targetDir, destName) at line 171; (2) trace via je.getName() -> substring -> destination (line 136) -> replace('/',separator) (line 139) -> destDir (line 140/145) -> targetDir = new File(dir, destDir) at line 155 -> new File(targetDir, destName) at line 171. Both converge on the unchecked write in copy(); the guard only exists in unjar()'s separate `target` computation (line 112-115), which is discarded and never actually used for the write path taken by copy().
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code, FileUtil.unjar(jis, extractRoot) accepts the crafted archive entry "../extractEVIL/pwned.txt" without throwing, and FileUtil.copy() writes a real file (content "PWNED-CONTENT") to <base>/extractEVIL/pwned.txt — a sibling directory of the intended extraction root <base>/extract, i.e. fully outside the sandboxed destination. The POV detects this by checking the escaped file's canonical path does not start with the extraction root's canonical path + separator, and exits 0. After a correct fix, the same archive causes unjar() to throw IOException ("... paths with .. characters") and no file is written at the escape location, so the POV exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: Targeted the alert's shared sink: both traces converge on FileUtil.copy() line 171 (`new File(targetDir, destName)`), reached either via the `name`/`destName` chain (trace 1) or the `destination`/`destDir`/`targetDir` chain (trace 2) — both are exercised simultaneously by a single crafted archive entry name, since both `name` and `destination` are derived from the same `je.getName()` split at the last '/'. I chose the sibling-directory-prefix bypass (root "extract" vs "extractEVIL") rather than a naive "../../etc/passwd" traversal because the naive case is already caught by the existing `target.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(dir.getCanonicalPath())` check and is already covered by the pre-existing `badExtractTest` in FileUtilTest.java — it would not actually reproduce the CVE-aligned "insufficient destination containment" flaw described in the alert note. The sibling-prefix case is the real, currently-unguarded bypass: it passes the existing check (due to missing separator boundary) yet still writes outside the extraction root, which is exactly what a complete fix must close. Verified experimentally: unpatched FileUtil -> POV exits 0 (escape succeeds); FileUtil patched with a separator-boundary-aware containment check -> POV exits 1 (unjar throws, no escape). No changes were made to product code or existing tests; only the new file under .security-pipeline/pov/ was added, and it compiles/runs standalone against FileUtil.java (which has no Karaf-specific compile dependencies) via javac/java inside the project's Docker image.
parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant a correct fix must enforce: for every archive entry, the final resolved write path (as used at FileUtil.java line 171, i.e. new File(targetDir, destName) after normalization/canonicalization) must be equal to, or a proper descendant of, the extraction root directory — checked with a separator-aware comparison (e.g. `canonical.equals(rootCanonical) || canonical.startsWith(rootCanonical + File.separator)`, or better, `Path.normalize()` + `Path.startsWith(Path)` on java.nio.file.Path, or verifying the resolved path's parent chain contains the root). A bare `String.startsWith(rootCanonicalPath)` without appending the separator is NOT sufficient and is exactly the bug (sibling-directory prefix collision, e.g. root "extract" vs "extractEVIL", or root "/opt/data" vs "/opt/data2"). The fix should be applied at (or reachable from) the actual write sink in copy() — not only in unjar()'s discarded `target` variable — so that any future/alternate caller of copy() (or a caller that bypasses unjar()'s check) is still protected. Known bypass variants the fix must also block: (a) sibling-prefix collision demonstrated here (`../<rootName>SUFFIX/...`); (b) plain `..` traversal escaping to unrelated paths (already caught by the existing check/tests, must remain blocked); (c) absolute paths (already checked via `getName().startsWith("/")`, but should also reject Windows-style absolute paths like `C:\...` or entries starting with `\\`); (d) traversal hidden via backslash separators on the raw entry name before the `'/'`→`File.separatorChar` replace (line 139) — e.g. an entry containing literal `..\\` sequences that only become meaningful after replacement, or mixed separators; (e) symlink-based escapes where a legitimately-contained path component is itself a symlink pointing outside the root (canonicalization handles this if performed on the fully resolved target, but must be re-validated after any directory creation via mkdirs()). Any patch should be regression-tested against: the existing `badExtractTest` (plain `..` traversal, must still throw), this POV's sibling-prefix case (must now throw / not escape), and ideally a symlink-escape case.
parsed_output.summary: Created a standalone Java POV (PathTraversalPOV.java) that drives the real, unmodified FileUtil.unjar()/FileUtil.copy() public API in org.apache.karaf.obr.command.util.FileUtil with a crafted in-memory JAR entry. The entry name "../extractEVIL/pwned.txt" traverses out of the extraction root and back into a sibling directory ("extractEVIL") that merely shares the same string prefix as the intended root ("extract"). Because FileUtil's containment check is a bare String.startsWith(dir.getCanonicalPath()) with no path-separator boundary, the sibling directory is wrongly accepted as "inside" the root, and copy() writes the file completely outside the extraction directory. Verified: on the current (unpatched) code the POV writes the file outside the root and exits 0; against a hand-patched copy of FileUtil.java that appends File.separator to the prefix check (equivalent to a real fix), unjar() throws IOException and rejects the archive, and the POV exits 1.

parsed_output.patch_notes: Root cause: FileUtil's only path-containment guard (in unjar(), line ~113) compared canonical paths with a bare String#startsWith and no separator boundary, so `extractEVIL` incorrectly passed as \"inside\" root `extract`. Worse, the validated `target` variable there was discarded — the actual write in copy() (`new File(targetDir, destName)`) was never re-validated, so any caller of copy() (or a bypass of unjar()'s check) was unprotected. Fix: added a private `checkContainment(File root, File target)` helper doing `canonicalTarget.equals(canonicalRoot) || canonicalTarget.startsWith(canonicalRoot + File.separator)`, used it to replace the broken check in unjar(), and added the same check in copy() on both `targetDir` (before mkdirs()) and the final resolved `targetFile` (before opening the FileOutputStream) — the true sink identified by both alert traces. Added `siblingPrefixExtractTest` reproducing the POV's sibling-directory-prefix bypass (`../extractEVIL/pwned.txt` against root `extract`) as a JUnit regression test alongside the existing `goodExtractTest`/`badExtractTest`, which continue to pass unchanged.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk: the change only tightens an existing security check to be separator-boundary-aware and adds an equivalent check at the write sink; it does not alter behavior for any legitimately-contained path (equal-to-root or proper-descendant paths still pass, since canonicalization does not require the file to exist). Verified: full obr module `mvn test` reactor build succeeds (11 modules, BUILD SUCCESS), existing goodExtractTest/badExtractTest plus the new siblingPrefixExtractTest all pass (3/3), and the provided POV now exits 1 (archive rejected, no file written outside the extraction root) versus exit 0 before the patch.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed a path-traversal (CWE-22) root cause in FileUtil.java where archive-entry-derived filenames reached FileUtil.copy()'s FileOutputStream sink without adequate containment validation. The only existing guard (in unjar()) used a bare String#startsWith(canonicalDir) comparison with no path-separator boundary, so a sibling directory whose name extends the root's name (e.g. root "extract" vs sibling "extractEVIL") passed the check while resolving outside the intended extraction root — and that guard's `target` variable was never actually used by the write path in copy() anyway. Replaced it with a shared `checkContainment(root, target)` helper that does a separator-aware canonical-path comparison (`equals(root) || startsWith(root + File.separator)`), applied it at unjar()'s existing check, and additionally applied it at copy()'s actual write sink (both on targetDir before mkdirs() and on the final resolved output file before FileOutputStream is opened) so both alert traces converging on `new File(targetDir, destName)` are covered, along with any future/alternate caller of copy() that bypasses unjar()'s check.
